0:00–0:15. Arescope is a prototype for unified rover mission control. Its target architecture connects rovers, their uncrewed home base on Mars and Earth Mission Control. Shared maps and Guardian warnings support the operator. Our current software demonstration runs on Earth.
The problem · Mars rover operations

Rover risks and delayed help

In 2009, Spirit broke through a thin crust into soft sand at Troy.

3–22 minEarth signal delay · one way
Dust, glare & low texture
Cameras lose reliable visual landmarks.
Wheel slip & obstruction
Motion can stall in soft terrain.
Sensor & link dropout
Missing data interrupts the mission view.

Arescope connects risk warnings, coordinated help and operator review.

NASA/JPL · Spirit at Troy
NASA · Mars communication delay

MER Spirit · Troy2009 · Hidden Trap
Illustrative overlay: visible surface only, no subsurface sensing.Click or press Enter to toggle the rover scan
Spirit broke through a thin crust at Troy in 2009. A signal takes 3–22 minutes one way between Earth and Mars. Dust, glare, low texture, wheel slip, obstructions, and sensor or link dropout can degrade mission awareness. Arescope joins risk warnings, coordinated assistance and reviewed learning. The Troy drawing is illustrative and does not claim hidden-soil detection or that Arescope would have saved Spirit. Sources: NASA/JPL Spirit’s View from Troy; NASA Speaking Percy’s Language; NASA Self-Driving Perseverance Takes the Wheel.

1:35–2:05. Describe three levels: protection on each rover, mission coordination at an uncrewed home base on Mars, and Earth Mission Control for oversight and reviewed learning. The Mars home base is the fleet's local compute and communications hub. Click the Earth-link buttons as an architecture illustration only. Current Guardian inference and coordination run in LAB. Physical base deployment, onboard inference and interplanetary store-and-forward behavior require further implementation and tests.

Synthetic hold-out: 36 trajectories, 1,152 windows. Baseline caught 26/30 faults, adapted model 30/30 after 192 reviewed synthetic windows. No field or flight validation.

The previous slide shows the simulated recovery workflow. These metrics describe an adapted Guardian model on a separate frozen synthetic hold-out, not a physical rover trial or the active production model. The baseline caught 26 of 30 faults; after reviewed synthetic adaptation, the model caught 30 of 30. Mean lead time is 14.8 seconds and false alarms cover 11 of 492 nominal windows. Model activation requires operator review.

AI use: AI assisted code and pitch drafting. Guardian uses ML. Voice Copilot uses an LLM with supplied telemetry. Operators review outputs and approve model activation. Field deployment remains future work.

2:45–3:00. Close on the Earth prototype and the next physical rover trial. The uncrewed Mars home base is the planned hub for rover coordination and Earth data relay. Future astronaut teams would join the same map and data network, toward a Mars surface internet shared by robots, bases and people. This is the long-term unification vision, not a deployed communications system. Minor-fault service is simulated; physical repair remains unvalidated. Disclose AI-assisted development, Guardian ML and operator Copilot.
